Consult Summary:
- Adult female with 6-day history of painful urination, malodorous urine, intermittent midline lower abdominal pain (7/10), and blood spots in urine; afebrile, no back/loin pain. Clinically consistent with uncomplicated lower UTI; empiric 3-day antibiotic course prescribed with hydration and safety-net advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful urination.
- Symptom details:
  - Onset/duration: 6 days.
  - Course: Ongoing; lower abdominal pain comes and goes.
  - Location: Lower abdomen, midline/suprapubic.
  - Severity: Pain rated 7/10.
  - Associated urinary symptoms: Malodorous urine; able to pass urine; blood spots in urine for 6 days.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No fever/feverishness.
  - No lower back or loin pain (initially ambiguous response; ultimately denies).
  - No vaginal discharge.
  - Eating and drinking normally.
  - No prior similar episodes; no known kidney problems; no prior UTIs.
  - Regular menstrual periods.
  - No recent triggers reported (no increased exercise, dehydration, or increased sexual activity).
- GI review:
  - Past IBS; denies change in bowel habit and weight loss.
  - When asked about blood in stool, patient referenced hematuria; subsequently denies bowel changes.
- Systems review: As above; otherwise not discussed.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS); no recent flare reported; no complications noted.
- Denies prior kidney problems or urinary infections.
- No prior surgeries reported.

Medications:
- Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily (regular use).
- New prescription: Antibiotic for presumed UTI (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); 3-day course planned.
- Allergies: Clindamycin.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with friends.
- Occupation: Support worker.
- Alcohol: Occasional; approximately one glass of wine per week.
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Illicit substances: Not discussed.

Family History:
- None reported.

Physical Examination:
- 

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Urine testing deferred; empirical treatment chosen.
- Advised to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature at home.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis) with dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and hematuria; afebrile; no flank/loin pain.
  - Plan:
    - Empiric oral antibiotic for 3 days; e-prescription sent to requested pharmacy (Knightsbridge Practice). Medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Increase oral fluids to 2.5–3 liters/day.
    - Optional supportive measures: cranberry juice; over-the-counter urinary alkalinizing sachets per pharmacy advice.
    - Obtain a home thermometer and monitor temperature.
    - Safety net: Seek care urgently if worsening pain, new lower back/loin pain, fever/high temperature, difficulty passing urine, or if symptoms fail to improve on antibiotics. If symptoms recur, reconsult for further evaluation.
    - No need to call after completing antibiotics if fully recovered.
- Issue 2: IBS, stable.
  - Plan: Continue Mebeverine 200 mg TID; no changes discussed.
- Issue 3: Medication allergy.
  - Plan: Documented clindamycin allergy; avoid clindamycin in prescribing.

General Plan items:
- Prescription to be available at pharmacy within ~1 hour; patient to collect and start as soon as possible.
- Written advice to be included in notes per clinician.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals not obtained; no physical exam; no urinalysis or urine culture; pregnancy status not discussed; antibiotic name/dose/route/frequency not documented; LMP/date not recorded; full sexual history not obtained.
- Internal conflicts: Initial ambiguous response regarding lower back pain; ultimately denies. Patient answered a GI bleeding question with hematuria; later denies bowel habit change or weight loss.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear with minor interruptions/unclear utterances; clinically sufficient information captured.
